A1.justification: Both PDFs describe G-DexGrasp and retain matching methods, equations, experiments, and figures. All pages are readable, including v2's added supplementary material; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original grasp-generation comparisons, simulation metrics, ablations, and a perceptual user study in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds seen-category comparisons and supplementary experiments on retrieval descriptors, diversity, parsing, open-set objects, and reduced supervision.

M1.justification: The main retrieval, CVAE generation, and two-stage optimization pipeline remains unchanged. Supplementary Section 3.2 adds an implemented retrieval variant using Basis Point Set features and cosine similarity instead of OBB-size distances, a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on filtered Objaverse-tiny objects pre-segmented by PartField, extending the original curated object coverage to another open-set population. Supplementary Section 3.1 also evaluates parsing and grounding with point and press added to the original five affordances; it does not establish full grasp-generation evaluation for those additional actions.

E2.justification: Main Table 1 retains AffordPose, GrabNet†, GraspTTA†, and Ours*. Supplementary Table 1 adds Ours-BPS as an internal comparison method against the original Ours-OBB. Newly cited AffordDexGrasp and Dexterous Grasp Transformer are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds held-out seen-category evaluation with a stated 8:1:1 AffordPose split, parsing/grounding metrics, and diversity metrics evaluated on the AffordPose test set. New protocols also filter and rescale the first 500 Objaverse-tiny candidates and test 30 intrinsic configurations per affordance or one-tenth extrinsic supervision. These are additional evaluation designs, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The supplement adds OBB-versus-BPS sensitivity testing, reduced-supervision scalability tests, five-versus-seven-affordance parsing analysis, and grasp-diversity analysis. A microwave case traces intermediate processing, while additional ablation visualizations examine penetration, contact, and initialization failures beyond v1's bucket example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new standard deviations of translation, rotation, and joint angles measure generated-grasp diversity, rather than uncertainty in reported performance. The stated 30-participant study size is unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 adds seen-category scores while preserving the original unseen-category values; for example, Ours now reports seen/unseen part accuracy of 82.6/71.6%. Main Table 2 is unchanged. Supplementary results add BPS comparisons, diversity, parsing accuracy, Objaverse-PartField, reduced-supervision settings, and a Fast Version row. These are newly reported results, not improvements under the original settings.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup, retrieval-distance definitions, and losses in Equations 1–7 remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the supplement adds empirical analyses without new formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval-augmented generalization, part-aware generation, and prior-guided refinement. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 3.3 newly explains the tradeoff between diversity and task-aligned, natural grasps, acknowledges room to improve joint-angle diversity, and justifies restricting diversity comparisons to seen categories. Other additions interpret descriptor and reduced-data results as evidence of flexibility and scalability. The original part-segmentation limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the full GPT-4o prompt and action definitions, plus user-study details including the 0–5 scale, two viewpoints, and 20 examples across 19 unseen categories. It also documents preprocessing and supervision settings for added experiments. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes v1's batch size of 90, and the Fast Version configuration remains unexplained.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges concurrent AffordDexGrasp in Section 2.2 and adds Dexterous Grasp Transformer to the data-driven literature. The supplement introduces citations for Objaverse, PartField, and BPS. These are limited additions; the main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally condenses related-work, method-overview, and dataset prose while retaining the main section organization. It adds acknowledgments and organized supplementary sections, updates affiliation ordering and equal-contribution markings, and makes bibliographic corrections. The existing narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Main Table 1 changes to paired seen/unseen entries with ranking colors based on their averages. The supplement adds three tables and five figures, including the prompt, survey screenshot, intermediate-stage visualization, and extensive comparison and ablation grids. Main figures are largely retained, with limited label corrections such as Figure 3's feature dimension.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central assumptions that v1 left largely untested: parsing reliability, retrieval-descriptor sensitivity, scalability with fewer labels, and generalization with automated segmentation on open-set objects. The disclosed prompt and user-study procedure also materially improve reproducibility. The removed batch-size disclosure and underspecified Fast Version and filtered Objaverse sample count are weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
